contract.fieldReference: Version2 public possible ranges: people[{suspectId,placeIds[6],toolIds[6],timeIds[6],routes[6]:{placeId,toolId,timeId}}], places[{placeId,toolIds[6],timeIds[6]}]. Paired rows must be read together; none identifies an actual event.

sourcePurposes.portrait: One observed person trait. It identifies neither a player nor a role.
sourcePurposes.access: A different person trait. Its case-specific resemblance pair varies among six category combinations.
sourcePurposes.scene: One structural feature limits the paired possible routes for people; it does not name the actual location.
sourcePurposes.tool: Six compatible tools limit paired routes. Exact-tool testimony can further narrow the evidence.
sourcePurposes.time: Six compatible 15-minute intervals limit paired routes. Exact-time testimony can further narrow the evidence.

ablationMethod.baseline: All five actual original-record snapshots plus D initial private observations and known-own innocence, using the same public fieldReference.
ablationMethod.sourceAblations: Remove originals in the given dimension and D private clues in that dimension; count cases that restore at least one person, not just more coordinate combinations.
ablationMethod.recordAblations: Remove only that original record, preserving all other original records and every D private clue; count cases that restore at least one person.
ablationMethod.comparison: The previous Cartesian-marginal model restored people in 0/500 cases for each place/tool/time dimension. Paired-route constraints replace that shortcut.

limits: These are deterministic bot-policy outcomes, not human win rates or a claim of optimal balance.
Both policies use only authenticated projected views. Evaluation reads actual truth only to count outcomes and invariant violations.
Originals-first reads all available original records before questioning; verified-observations-first questions a volunteered observation while a kit remains, audits it, then returns to originals.
The crime policy knows only its permitted caseSecret, deters lies while a public kit remains, then spends only legal shared lies. It guesses seal categories without raw record access.
S uses two memories, then makes one private DAY4 report based on projected candidates and unverified voluntary observations. No correct-answer feedback is available.

All-record sweep deliberately grants all five originals for information-pressure analysis. It leaves at least three public people including C/S; adding initial D observations and known-own innocence still leaves at least two and retains S.

Generation preserves a possible route for C, S and a third person under all originals and initial D observations. Other routes are sampled from coherent permissions/ranges. This is a constrained puzzle model, not physical forensic simulation.

A possible route means an exhaustive in-game compatibility option, not a confirmed visit, actual use, proved alibi or causal forensic finding. Public data never labels which possible event actually happened.

Each partial source narrows person possibilities in some cases. No source dimension is claimed necessary in every case; duplicate or already-sufficient observations can make an individual record redundant.
Restricting generation to four-person resemblance groups was rejected: it would reduce six resemblance category pairs to two and make S partners deterministic for eight of twelve culprit profiles.
Free-text chat can contain arbitrary deception; these policies model one volunteered observation per seat and are not conversational agents.
Search repetition never yields additional constraints. A kit certifies statement truth only, including twelve-valued tool/time claims.
